channel.title: Wire — Frontend
channel.description: Frontend from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: Josh Comeau's The Future of CSS
item.description: Every year, browser vendors collaborate via the Interop project to synchronize their efforts on new HTML/CSS/JS features. This year, there’s a ton of super exciting features being considered! (3 sources: frontendfocus, hackernews, lobsters)

item.title: Upcoming Critical PHP Security Release
item.description: PHP is a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers everything from your blog to the most popular websites in the world. (2 sources: frontendfocus, lobsters)

item.title: Do Web Components Have a Future If Nobody is Writing Them?
item.description: With my previous post on “using the platform”, I was surprised that the comments on Hacker News and Lobsters tended to veer toward web components. This… (3 sources: frontendfocus, javascriptweekly, lobsters)

item.title: Chartist 2.0: The Lightweight SVG Charting Library Returns
item.description: Simple, responsive charts drawn in SVG and styled with CSS. Tiny, typed, and happy without a build step. (2 sources: frontendfocus, javascriptweekly)

item.title: Pele: Mermaid Diagrams as Lightweight, Themeable SVG
item.description: Pele is a lightweight open source library that renders Mermaid diagrams to SVG, themed with CSS variables. (2 sources: frontendfocus, javascriptweekly)

item.title: Try the playground
item.description: Edit diagrams and compare Pele with Mermaid. (2 sources: frontendfocus, javascriptweekly)

item.title: what it's able to render in under 100 bytes
item.description: JXL art gallery with links to source code. Procedural images as tiny JPEG XL files (SDR). (2 sources: frontendfocus, javascriptweekly)

item.title: Vercel Labs Open-Sources fx: A Zig Coding Agent Designed to Be Embedded
item.description: Vercel Labs has released fx, an experimental open-source coding agent written in Zig. It runs as a CLI, a script component, or an embedded library, including a WebAssembly build. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: go/ links that live in a file in your repo (open source)
item.description: Chrome and Firefox extension that does this for your twigg repository. The links are defined in a GOLINKS file at the root of the repo, one alias per line. Add a line, push, submit and done. No admin page, and changes are versioned. (1 source: rprogramming)
